summary: The talk opens with a relatable scenario: performance complaints from product are met with engineering's honest answer that investigation time is unpredictable—ranging from an hour to weeks—and only specific people like "Dave" understand legacy code. The speaker frames this as a "leaky bucket" cycle where issues are ignored until crisis, fixed in emergency mode, then return to neglect. Google's 2026 Dora metrics add context: AI increases individual effectiveness but also software delivery instability, while throughput remains largely unchanged. The proposed solution is an automated agentic workflow running weekly with real production context, scoring high-ROI opportunities by complexity and impact. The system provides evidence by implementing fixes, rerunning tests, and verifying impact before presenting results for human review. Infrastructure is vendor-neutral across compute, harness, and model; secure in tool calls and authentication; triggerable via scheduled runs or webhooks; and maintainable with feedback loops, using GitHub Actions, Claude Code, MCP, and Slack. Three early hurdles emerged: plausible-but-unverified fixes, complex ClickHouse queries, and lazy exception-handling. A deeper context gap existed between service-level metrics and function-level agent reasoning, solved by 'prod-to-code' translation connecting endpoints, event consumers, and cron jobs to functions, capturing forensic evidence only for requests exceeding P99 thresholds. To reduce eval variance, structured skills were added—e.g., understanding where HTTP 500 errors originated or comparing memory spikes to baselines. Automations built on top include auto-fixing issues, detecting dead code inactive for 60+ days, and the performance optimization pipeline targeting artificial delays, N+1 queries, missing indexes, and sequential assigns. The naive approach of opening many PRs failed because no one wants to review 80 PRs. Instead, the system prioritizes by hot-path frequency, business criticality (payments, sign-ups), would-the-PM-prioritize-it reasoning, and risk (migrations needed), surfacing only highest-ROI items. Reports are human-friendly gists explaining the issue and fix concisely, letting engineers create tickets or PRs themselves. Starting with one report at a time built appetite and trust. Four lessons: define what matters via scoring and guardrails; the real value is automating a phase that never happened before—not just doing existing work faster; context over cleverness consistently wins; and autonomous agentic automation requires 80-90% trust, dramatically different from using an agent interactively in an IDE where 80% success is acceptable because the human is in the loop.

sections.title: The Performance Investigation Problem
sections.summary: The speaker opens with a relatable scenario of product reporting slow pages and engineering unable to estimate investigation time—somewhere between an hour and a week. Only specific individuals like 'Dave' understand legacy code, creating a bottleneck. The speaker introduces themselves and their company building a runtime intelligence layer for coding agents that captures function-level and forensic context.

sections.title: AI Adoption Reality and Dora Metrics
sections.summary: Google's 2026 Dora metrics show the biggest AI impact is individual effectiveness, but the second is software delivery instability—throughput remains largely unchanged while software breaks more often. The speaker frames this as a gap between the promise of the AI revolution and current reality.

sections.title: Vision: Automated Performance Investigation
sections.summary: The 'leaky bucket' problem: issues are ignored until crisis, fixed in emergency mode, then return to neglect. The research phase is a black box with unpredictable ROI. The vision is to automate investigation weekly with real production context, flagging high-ROI opportunities scored by complexity and impact.

sections.title: Infrastructure and Workflow Implementation
sections.summary: Infrastructure requirements include vendor-neutrality, security, trigger systems, and maintainability with feedback loops. Implementation uses GitHub Actions running weekly, Claude Code, MCP for runtime intelligence, and Slack for reports. The agent analyzes production context, scores opportunities, and provides evidence by fixing, rerunning tests, and verifying impact before human review.

sections.title: Challenges and Prod-to-Code Context
sections.summary: Three hurdles: 'plausible unverified' fixes; complex ClickHouse queries; and 'lazy fixes' catching exceptions instead of root-causing. A deeper context problem exists between service-level metrics and function-level reasoning. The 'prod-to-code' approach translates production intelligence to function-level context, connecting endpoints, event consumers, and cron jobs to functions, capturing forensic evidence only for requests exceeding P99.

sections.title: Skills, Automations, and Prioritization
sections.summary: Structured skills were added to reduce eval variance—e.g., tracing HTTP 500 origins or comparing memory spikes to baselines. Automations built on top include auto-fixing issues, detecting dead code inactive 60+ days, and performance optimization targeting artificial delays, N+1 queries, missing indexes, and sequential assigns. Opening many PRs failed because no one wants 80 PRs. Instead, the system prioritizes by hot-path frequency, business criticality, PM-would-prioritize reasoning, and risk, surfacing only highest-ROI items as human-friendly report gists.

sections.title: Lessons Learned and Trust Thresholds
sections.summary: Four lessons: (1) Define what matters—scoring and guardrails make automation reliable. (2) The real value is automating a phase that never happened before, not just accelerating existing work. (3) Context over cleverness—right context and skills consistently outperform relying on model intelligence. (4) Autonomous agentic automation requires 80-90% trust, dramatically different from interactive IDE use where 80% success is acceptable because the human is in the loop. The hardest part was reaching sufficient confidence that issues are worth fixing and fixes are verified in runtime before handing to human reviewers.
